one_line_contribution: From a single pool of ALFWorld episodes, materialize a GEPA-optimized instruction and an ExpeL-style retrieval store, move both unchanged to other backbones, and show that the instruction's marginal gain decays more than the store's and that the negative instruction-by-store interaction (the 'substitution' this program keeps measuring on one backbone) is a property of the (backbone, optimizer) pair rather than of the episodes.
closest_prior_work: MemoHarness (arXiv:2607.14159, verified via the literature command, hf channel) is the sharpest threat: it evolves an agent harness from execution experience and already reports *selective* transfer to unseen base models — i.e. that some of an evolved textual artifact is backbone-bound and some is not, which is the proposal's model-shaped/task-shaped dichotomy in embryo. It does not separate an instruction channel from a memory channel or report an interaction term, so the 2x2 and the differential contrast D survive. Second threat, instruction side: PromptBridge (arXiv:2512.01420, verified, s2+hf) exists precisely because optimized prompts do not survive a model switch, and MePO (arXiv:2505.09930, verified) is built on the premise that prompt quality has a model-agnostic and a model-specific part; between them, half of P1 ('the instruction loses under transfer') is closer to established background than to a finding. Store side: MemCollab (arXiv:2603.23234 — I verified it on Semantic Scholar with 5 citations, contradicting the proposal's claim that it 'was not found on S2 or HF') and Agent Memory Distillation (arXiv:2608.07169, verified) both move a memory across heterogeneous backbones and implicitly assume it is task-shaped. Also relevant and uncited: 'Teach Better or Show Smarter?' (arXiv:2406.15708, verified) is the instruction-vs-exemplar attribution study for prompt optimization; a reviewer will ask why its conclusions do not already predict the ordering here. Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666, verified) makes the task-shaped assertion but never tests a swap, so the proposal's framing of it is accurate. Net: no single paper owns the claim, but the predicted direction is the field's working assumption, which caps how much a confirmatory result can be worth.
strongest_objection: D = L_I - L_S is not scale-free, so P1 can be confirmed by arithmetic rather than by shape. Transfer loss is defined as a drop in a marginal gain, and a channel with a larger source-side gain has strictly more to lose; GEPA on ALFWorld routinely moves success by many points while this program's own pilot found the retrieval channel gave zero-to-negative gain and required volume control to stop it hurting. In the plausible regime Delta_S(A,A) is near zero, L_S is then near zero by construction, and D >= 4 points passes with no evidence whatsoever about 'shape'. The reverse-direction control (B to A) fixes a capability-gap artifact, not this: it is the same estimator applied twice. The paper's whole mechanism story rests on a contrast that is confounded with source-side effect size. A second, near-equal objection: D is a third-order contrast (a difference of differences of differences over eight cells per block), but the pre-registered MDE of 3-4 points is computed from a pairwise discordance rate at 400 tasks x 2 seeds. The standard error on D is substantially larger than on a paired cell difference, so a 4-point threshold with a bootstrap CI excluding zero is very likely underpowered, and the honest outcome is an uninformative wide interval rather than either the prediction or the stated null. Third: the clause-level analysis labels a clause model-shaped from the A-vs-B baseline failure-frequency ratio and then tests it by ablating on A and B (P3). The label is fit on exactly the backbone difference the ablation is supposed to reveal, so if clause targeting works at all the asymmetry is close to tautological; the informative version would fix labels from A alone (e.g. by which failure category a clause was introduced to fix in the GEPA trace) and let B be a genuine prediction.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Make the primary estimand scale-free: report retention R = Delta(target)/Delta(source) per channel with a bootstrap CI on the ratio difference, and add a gain-matched arm — a truncated or weakened instruction whose source-side Delta_I(A,A) equals Delta_S(A,A) within noise — so that 'the instruction loses more' cannot be read off the source-side gains. Pre-register a floor (e.g. Delta_S(A,A) >= 4 points on A) below which the whole comparison is declared degenerate and reported as such. (2) Re-derive the MDE for D itself by simulation from the pilot discordance rates, not for a pairwise cell, and be explicit that the confirmatory run may be powered only for the ratio contrast and not for the interaction shift in P2. (3) Fix the clause labels from the source side only (which failure category the GEPA reflection trace names when it introduces the clause), and treat B's baseline failure distribution as held-out evidence rather than as the labeling input. (4) Cut the matrix: the k x {raw, insight} x source-B cross is what makes the budget implausible; run the full 2x2 for three targets x one source plus a single reverse-direction block, and demote k and representation to one target. (5) Report the interaction with its own null replicate, since omega is a fourth-difference and the program's own history says re-scoring alone moves headline numbers.
missing_baseline: A cheap-adaptation arm between 'carry unchanged' and 'fully re-optimize'. The plan's cost axis has only two poles (carry I_sigma, or pay for I_T from scratch), and the practitioner conclusion it advertises — which artifact to keep when the backbone changes, and how to reprice re-optimization — is not decidable without the middle option: a PromptBridge- or MePO-style transfer/rewrite of I_A for the target, or a warm-started GEPA on the target seeded with I_A at a small fraction of the 600-rollout budget. If a 60-rollout warm start recovers most of L_I, then the model-shaped/task-shaped distinction, whatever its sign, has little practical consequence and the paper's payoff evaporates. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also raise: an instruction optimized on a disjoint task split of A (model-shaped but not episode-shaped) as the clean separator between 'shaped by the backbone' and 'shaped by these episodes', and a target-native store S_T ceiling reported at the same place as the I_T ceiling.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. My queries, all answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace, both channels reporting ok; WebSearch and WebFetch were unavailable in this session, so channel (b) answered nothing): (1) 'optimized instruction transfer across backbones versus experience memory store transfer LLM agent' — 21 hits, nearest MemCollab 2603.23234, 2604.27003, 2608.15008, EvoAgentBench 2607.05202, 2606.04536, 2605.30690; none runs an instruction arm against a store arm. (2, --recent) 'prompt optimized on one model transferred to another model memory bank interaction ablation' — 7 hits, PromptBridge 2512.01420, MePO 2505.09930, JTPRO 2604.19821; no memory arm in any. (3, --recent) 'optimized prompts are model-specific gains do not transfer to a different LLM backbone' — 8 hits, adds 2505.02273 (Demystifying optimized prompts), 2505.09666, 2605.29678; instruction-side only. (4) 'Compiled Memory Atlas instruction compilation backbone swap portability of compiled experience' — returned only name-collision noise (ATLAS 2608.15546 and serving-systems papers); empty for this purpose, which I report as empty. (5, --recent) 'does agent experience memory transfer across different base models portability of learned experience' — MemHarness 2607.28272, Echo 2604.05533, MCMA 2601.07470 ('structured and transferable agent memory', frozen task model), 2604.27003; store-side only. (6) 'interaction between optimized system instruction and retrieved experience ALFWorld 2x2 matched token budget substitution' — nearest is 2406.15708 (instructions vs exemplars in APO); no backbone swap. (7, --recent) 'self-evolved agent context experience reused by a different backbone model whose gains are model specific' — S3Gym 2608.31100, UCE 2606.02304, MemEvolve 2512.18746; none. ID verification: I verified 2603.15666 (Atlas), 2607.14159 (MemoHarness), 2603.23234 (MemCollab), 2512.01420 (PromptBridge), 2601.18847 (MulVul), 2608.07169 (Agent Memory Distillation), 2607.11944 (MAGE), 2510.23730, 2605.30785 (AdaCoM — its capability-dependent fidelity/reliability trade-off does support the proposal's characterization), 2604.27003, 2507.19457 (GEPA) and 2608.04336 (COMPAS); every ID the novelty argument leans on resolved with a matching title, and I additionally resolved the proposal's unnamed 2607.28272 as MemHarness ('Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed'), which reduces negative transfer by training a reconstruction policy and is worth citing. I did not attempt the WebSearch-only IDs 2606.06448, 2603.07670, 2605.30842 or 2606.23127, so those remain unverified here. Judgement of the check itself: it is one of the more honest ones I have seen — five documented queries with IDs, explicit channel accounting, and named nearest neighbours rather than a bare 'no collision' — but it contains one factual error (MemCollab is on Semantic Scholar; it is not WebSearch-only) and one unresolved title it should have chased, and it does not search the framing under which a collision is most likely, namely 'model-agnostic vs model-specific prompt content' (MePO, 2505.02273), where the instruction half of the hypothesis is already close to received wisdom.
